question: Who was the Prime Minister when Right to Property was scrapped as a Fundamental Right?
solution:
The correct answer is __Morarji Desai.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• E arlier in India, the Right to Property was a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution.
 
• The right to property was described in Article 31 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• But by the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978), the right to property was converted from a fundamental right to a legal right.
 
• At present, the Right to Property is established as a legal right under Article 300(A) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Morarji Desai was the Prime Minister of India after the Emergency in the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• It is taken from the Constitution of the United States of America.
 
• Its description is in **Part 3**** **of the Constitution (Article 12 to Article 35).
 
• Indian citizens have the following fundamental rights:
 
 
• Equality or Right to Equality (Article 14 to Article 18)
 
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19 to 22)
 
• Right against exploitation (Articles 23 to 24)
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25 to 28)
 
• Right to Culture and Education (Articles 29 to 30)
 
• Constitutional Rights (Article 32)
 
 
 
• It can be amended and during a national emergency (Article 352), other fundamental rights can be suspended except the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• There were seven fundamental rights in the original constitution, but by the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978 AD).
 
• The right to property (Article 31 to Article 19f) was removed from the list of fundamental rights and placed as a legal right under Article 300 (a) of the Constitutio
